decisions.reason: The revision covers evaluative information as well as comments, with the retained trainer/presentation example selecting ordinary response information. Both selected passages show B2. The noun stays uncountable and separate from signal feedback or feed back.

The bounded schedule-change example selects ordinary authority-given allowance. Retain editorial A2 with Oxford A2 and Collins B1 preserved literally. This does not accept software access settings, written permission documents or consent validity.

The assigned-duty meaning is clear, and one of my responsibilities naturally illustrates a countable duty without adding a plural answer form. Collins assigned duties B2 supports the proposed course placement. Blame, liability and actual authority remain separate.

The welcome-pack example selects a concrete work item. Retain A2 supported by Oxford, with the Collins B2 disagreement explicit. Difficulty and membership of a larger project are not necessary conditions. Computing task processes are excluded.

The revised person-or-group definition accommodates a department while retaining organizational function. Collins B2 supports the placement; actor A2/B1+ evidence is excluded. Neither work titles nor this lexical acceptance establish authority or professional competence.

Retain the existing relative-importance definition and high-priority delivery example. Accept B2 as an independent editorial placement for comparison and work ordering, with no selected-source CEFR claim. Countable important-item B2 and traffic C2 are other senses; no operational priority policy is accepted.

The revision directly includes places where activities occur and matches meeting location. Accept editorial B1 using Oxford selected B1 while preserving Collins literal B1+ and its separate exact-position B2. Logical file or memory locations remain separate.

Postal or physical-location details can be spoken, so removing necessarily written improves precision. Retain the A2 course floor while preserving selected Collins A1. Electronic addresses and verbal address remain outside scope, and the ambiguous invitation expression stays held.

The retained characteristic written-name definition and form example match the ordinary noun. Collins B1 supports placement. Signing acts, stamps, electronic authentication, style and prescription senses receive no acceptance; no legal effect is inferred.

The retained shared-standard-time-region definition matches ordinary cross-location scheduling. Oxford selected B2 supports placement. Simplified 24-zone or universal one-hour-offset claims are excluded; no actual conversion or daylight-saving rule is approved.

source.title: 43-4051.00 - Customer Service Representatives
source.scope: The 2026 occupation page was consulted for communication, recordkeeping, billing, complaint referral, and work coordination. source.scope: Product-specific context for case statuses, ownership, reopening, and follow-up tickets. The source distinguishes solved from closed and explains system-controlled closure. source.title: About native Support time duration metrics
source.scope: Product-specific context for first reply, resolution, and waiting intervals. Native metrics and SLA metrics can use different behavior despite identical names. Counts, start/end events, exclusions, business hours, and other measures require explicit local definitions.

source.scope: UK data-protection context for sufficient, relevant, purpose-limited information. The page explicitly says it is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act and may change. source.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
source.scope: Context for impersonation, pressure, remote-access requests, and fake service or refund claims. The draft teaches reporting and approved contact routes, not scam scripts, credential collection, incident-response techniques, or universal payment-reversal rights.

source.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
source.scope: Occupational context for schedules, correspondence, records, office tools, supplies, and varied administrative roles. source.title: General Office Clerks

source.title: 43-6014.00 - Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive

source.scope: Audience, confidentiality-versus-privilege, consent and authorized disclosure, information sharing, and support-staff context consulted. Updated June 30, 2022. Applies to SRA-regulated England and Wales practice. The source excludes specific data-protection rights, processing bases, and retention advice. Disclosure exceptions and safeguarding examples are not taught as permission or procedure. Linked Codes, cases, other guidance, and assets were not reviewed or acquired.

source.title: Court Records
source.publisher: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
source.scope: Overview body consulted for case files, dockets, documents, PACER access versus CM/ECF electronic filing, and record/access context. Linked registration, filing, access rules, fees, retention schedules, and forms were not read or adopted. The overview does not establish that all court records are public or that a record is complete or authentic. No assets acquired.

source.title: Conflicts of interest
source.scope: Audience, own-interest conflict, competing client duties, prospective clients, information barriers, and safeguards context consulted. Updated March 2, 2020. SRA-regulated England and Wales practice only; no exception, consent, or checklist is treated as authorization to act. Linked Codes, case studies, and assets were not reviewed or acquired.

source.title: Civil Procedure Rules glossary
source.scope: Selected body passages consulted for affidavit, alternative dispute resolution, counterclaim, cross-examination, damages, injunction, limitation period, official copy, privilege, seal, service, set aside, stay, and without prejudice. The glossary guides existing meanings and does not create legal meaning. England and Wales civil context; the page displays January 30, 2017 update. Linked rules, forms, time calculations, legal validity assessments, and assets were not reviewed or adopted.

source.title: Leading question
source.scope: Entry body consulted for question wording that suggests an answer. Last reviewed June 2023. U.S. reference context; its permissibility discussion is not taught as a universal rule or questioning instruction. Linked Rule 611 and other entries were not opened. No source examples or assets are copied or acquired.

source.title: Circumstantial evidence
source.scope: Entry body consulted for support through inference rather than a direct account of the fact at issue. Last reviewed January 2022. U.S. reference context; the illustrative discrimination scenario is not copied or adopted, and no legal conclusion, proof threshold, or comparative weight is asserted. Linked entries and assets were not acquired.

source.title: Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 801
source.scope: Actual Rule 801(a)-(d) text consulted for statement, statement-maker, current trial or hearing, asserted-truth purpose, and the existence of exclusions. U.S. federal scope only. No admissibility determination, exception advice, advocacy method, or universal evidence rule is taught. Advisory notes and linked cases are not used as course evidence; no assets acquired.

source.title: Counterpart: origin and dictionary senses
source.scope: Origin passage and legal copy/duplicate sense consulted for the pending counter- plus part analysis. The origin links counter- and part; this does not validate every legal use or deeper morphology. News examples, illustrations, and linked resources are not copied or acquired. Dictionary consultation is not asset permission or qualified linguistic approval.

source.title: Counter- prefix senses
source.scope: Counter- prefix section consulted for corresponding/complementary and duplicate/substitute senses, distinct from the physical counter noun. This supports only the pending counterpart analysis and is not a general approval of all counter forms. Source images, examples, and linked pages are not copied or acquired.

source.title: Witnesses: Oaths, paragraphs 14-20
source.scope: Oaths paragraphs 14-20 consulted for the religious oath versus nonreligious affirmation distinction and respect for individual preference. England and Wales coroner context only. No age rule, ritual, prescribed wording, attendance process, or universal procedural requirement is taught. Linked legislation and guidance were not read, and no assets or quoted forms acquired.

source.title: Stripe: Billing addresses
source.scope: Selected passage: What is a billing address?; invoicing needs; shipping-address distinction. The address is associated with a payment account and billing records. It serves a different purpose from a delivery address and can differ from it. Limits: Payment-provider explanation only. No fraud judgment, mandatory address collection, verification procedure or legal requirement is inferred.

source.title: Adyen: Create an authorisation
source.scope: Selected passage: Response authCode field. The response has an authorization code after successful authorization and an empty field when authorization fails. The field is a transaction reference, not a customer PIN. Limits: One API field supports the selected meaning; the code is not proof of capture, settlement or payout. No card data or live processing is involved.

source.title: Adyen: Payments lifecycle
source.scope: Selected passage: Authorization statuses; Capture and settlement statuses. Authorization reserves funds and is distinct from capture and settlement. A refused request is not approved; later statuses must be checked separately. Limits: Provider-specific lifecycle explanation, not operational instructions or a universal status model. No code alone establishes final payment.

source.title: Shopify: Return merchandise authorization
source.scope: Consultation method: selected_page_passage. Selected passage: Definition and What is an RMA number?. A return process can require approval and assign a reference number to an approved return. The reference helps identify the return; it does not by itself guarantee a particular remedy. Limits: Provider explanation only. No universal RMA requirement, return period, packaging condition or override of consumer rights is adopted.

source.title: GOV.UK: Accepting returns and giving refunds
source.scope: Consultation method: selected_page_passage. Selected passage: Faulty goods, unwanted goods and distance-sales distinctions. The guidance distinguishes faulty products from change-of-mind returns and contains rights that depend on the circumstances. Packaging can be evidence of purchase rather than a universal condition for a remedy. Limits: Jurisdictional boundary check only. No deadlines, refund guarantees, original-packaging requirement or merchant discretion overriding legal rights is imported.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: The relevant consent arrangements for taking, storing, or using a person's images for stated purposes.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The team checked the scope of photo consent before the planned use.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Photo consent has purpose/use scope and separate privacy requirements; a permission slip does not substitute for it.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: A form used to request or record permission for a specified activity.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The permission slip identifies the planned activity.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: A permission slip requests or records allowance. It is a document and does not itself prove valid consent.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: Authorization of an internal request for a job position.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The requisition approval is still pending.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Requisition approval concerns an internal position request; it is neither hiring permission in every case nor acceptance of a candidate.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: Information given to a candidate about their application or assessment.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The recruiter explained when candidate feedback would be available.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Candidate feedback is response information about application/assessment, without certifying employment criteria or decisions.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: Authorization to use a specified resource or information.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The manager requested a review of the access permission.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Access permission is resource-specific authorization, distinct from identity authentication and organizational-role labels.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: The sequence of roles through which an approval request passes.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The request follows the stated approval chain.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: An approval chain sequences required decision roles; the chain alone is not permission or a completed approval.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: A table showing how responsibilities for activities are assigned to roles.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The responsibility matrix identifies who will provide the update.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: A responsibility matrix maps work duties to roles; it is a table and does not establish that its allocations are valid.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: Acceptance of a material for a defined project use through the applicable review process.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The material approval covers only the stated product and application.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Material approval is limited acceptance for a defined product/application, not broad permission or a generic priority decision.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: Acceptance of a submitted sample under defined criteria and scope.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The sample approval records the agreed finish reference.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Sample approval has particular criteria and scope; it does not certify every later supplied material.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: A record of what use or action was permitted and its relevant scope.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The permission record identifies the approved image use.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: A permission record describes allowance and scope, not the allowance act itself or proof of current valid consent.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: The current state of a required approval.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The approval status is still pending.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Approval status is the current recorded state, not an authorization decision or guarantee of completion.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: Authorization of content for a stated use.
related_entry_boundaries.example: Content approval is required before this page is published.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Content approval covers a stated use and actual process; ordinary permission does not supply publishing authority.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: A planned cycle of comments and response on work.
related_entry_boundaries.example: This feedback round covers the layout and wording.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: A feedback round is a planned cycle of response, not the comments themselves or approval of the work.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: The ending of a previously given agreement to an action or purpose, subject to the applicable context and requirements.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The record documents the withdrawal of consent and the subsequent discussion.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Withdrawal of consent concerns ending an agreement with context-specific effects, not simply revoking a software permission.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: A stamp that reproduces a person's signature.
related_entry_boundaries.example: Use of the signature stamp requires the applicable authorization.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: A signature stamp reproduces a mark; it is a device whose authorized use and legal effect remain unaccepted.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: A boundary on a person's authority to approve an amount or action.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The request exceeds this approver's stated approval limit.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: An approval limit bounds authority by amount or action, rather than being the permission itself.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: A table showing which roles may authorize particular actions under stated conditions.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The authorization matrix identifies the required role for this request.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: An authorization matrix records which roles may authorize under conditions; organizational role language does not validate the matrix.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: An address designated for service of legal documents under the applicable arrangements.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The reviewer will confirm the service address in the record.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: A service address is designated under legal-service arrangements; its formal validity cannot be inferred from ordinary postal meaning.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: A court order reflecting the parties' agreement as approved by the court under the applicable process.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The consent order must be distinguished from the parties' earlier draft agreement.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: A consent order is a court order under a process, distinct from parties' agreement, generic permission or a signature alone.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: Authorization required to bring an appeal in a process that imposes that requirement.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The lawyer will check whether permission to appeal is required.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Permission to appeal is process-specific authorization requiring legal review; the ordinary noun does not determine whether it is needed.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: The transfer of specified legal rights to another party under applicable law.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The proposed assignment requires review of the rights involved.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Assignment here transfers legal rights, not an assigned duty or work task.

related_entry_boundaries.definition: An obligation arising from a professional role and its applicable rules.
related_entry_boundaries.example: The lawyer will explain the relevant professional duty.
related_entry_boundaries.individual_observation: Professional duty depends on role and applicable rules; it is not merely any assigned task and does not establish competence.

consultations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: feedback
consultations.section: Uncountable response-information sense1 and selected topic, lines103-139; electrical sense2 line142
consultations.finding: The selected feedback concerns advice, evaluation or information about work and its usefulness. It is uncountable, with give/receive and on/from patterns. B2 appears on the selected suggestions/advice topic. Electrical noise and returning a signal are separate meanings.
consultations.limits: AI author consultation only. No dictionary text, audio, images or license acquired. Selected-sense labels are literal observations, separate from editorial course levels. Other senses, footer words, OPAL membership and frequency bands do not supply selected difficulty. Independent acceptance remains pending.

consultations.section: COBUILD sense1 lines222-228 and electrical sense2 lines230-231; British contrasts lines264-306

consultations.limits: AI author consultation only. No dictionary text, audio, images or license acquired. Selected-sense labels are literal observations, separate from editorial course levels.
